headline: Europe Is Zelenskyy’s Only Ally Now, Latvian Leader Says
author: Aaron Eglitis and Oliver Crook

paragraphs.text: Fri, October 16, 2026 at 1:57 AM CDT 1 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has only one ally now and that's Europe, the Latvian prime minister said, referring to Kyiv's spiraling tensions with the US.

The Ukrainian president is set to meet European Union leaders in Brussels on Friday, just days after he said he felt betrayed by Donald Trump over a diesel deal with Russia and temporary restrictions placed on intelligence assistance.

"We see that Zelenskyy has only one ally now, it's actually the Europeans," Kulbergs told Bloomberg TV in an interview. "The most important thing that we're going to discuss today is what he needs for this winter. It's all about this winter."

In the span of a week, Trump has trashed years of energy sanctions on the Kremlin in a bid to lower energy prices ahead of Nov. 3 midterm elections, pressured Kyiv to quit bombing Russian oil refineries and suggested Zelenskyy should step aside as president.
'We also have to understand that the United States is now running into the midterms. It's election time," Kulbergs said. "That's a different vibe."
